newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline retains firm tone, U.S still the draw.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline retains firm tone, U.S still the draw.

text.p: NWE gasoline was a touch firmer on Thursday with demand once again from the U.S.
Eurograde barges traded between $219-223.75 fob ARA, up $1 or so despite NYMEX gasoline losing some ground.

Traders said the big freeze gripping much of Europe meant the location of barges in the region which has been hit by forzen canals has become all important. Shell has said it is using trucks to transport material.
On cargoes a 10,000 tonne Eurograde parcel was sold at $220.50 fob Gothenburg loading January 20-25. Some thought this parcel might be used as a top up to a transatlantic cargo.
Tankers have become increasingly hard to find and players expected to pay high levels to move their cargoes.

A 5,000 tonne piece of Russian A95 grade was sold at $250 cif Riga arriving by January 15. Traders said the high price of the material, which is similar to Eurograde, reflected high freight rates to the port and significant discharge costs.
Swaps were about $2 stronger with Jan barge swaps talked $223-224 fob ARA.
